title: Opportunity
description: A Programme offered for a particular intake, campus and teaching language. This is the smallest thing a student can actually assess or save, and the unit the whole product is built around.

instruction.description: The language the Programme is actually taught in.

fullyInLanguage.description: False where only part of the degree is in this language — a common and consequential trap.

restricted.description: True where meeting the requirements does not guarantee a place.

selection.description: How eligible applicants are ranked. Kept computationally separate from eligibility — a cut-off is not a requirement.

historicalCutoffs.description: Past cut-offs are context for how competitive something has been. They are never treated as a requirement and never used to predict an offer.

requirements.description: Machine-readable rules paired with the source's own wording.

officialRequirementsText.description: The requirement paragraph as published, kept verbatim so a counsellor can audit our normalisation.

cost.description: One entry per applicant group, because the same Opportunity costs different people very different amounts.

priceYear.description: The academic year the figure was published for. Required honesty: never present an old figure as current.

mandatory.description: False marks a Selection Factor — used in ranking, not in eligibility.

ibSubject.description: For kind 'ib-subject'. An IB subject id or name from data/ib-subjects.json. This is the default way to write a requirement and it needs no Recognition Scheme: the source said HL and the student has HL, so there is nothing to translate.

ibLevel.description: For kind 'ib-subject'. HL, SL, or 'any' where the source accepts either.

subject.description: For kind 'local-equivalency'. A subject name in the vocabulary of the scale named by `levelScale` — the source's own word, not ours.

levelScale.description: For kind 'local-equivalency'. The id of the subject scale `level` is measured on, matching a Recognition Scheme's subjectScale.id. A level with no scale is a number with no unit: 'A' means the top of three levels in one country and the top of five in another, and a requirement that does not say which cannot be checked.

level.description: For kind 'local-equivalency'. A level code the scale named by `levelScale` defines.

minGrade.description: On the scale named by `gradeScale` for a local-equivalency rule, or the IB's own 1-7 scale for an ib-subject rule. On an ib-course-results rule it is the IB grade every subject in the award must reach, not one named subject.

minGradeWaivedAtLevel.description: For a local-equivalency rule with a minGrade: the level on the same scale at which the minimum no longer applies — ITU and CBS publish "no grade requirement if [the subject] at A-level is passed". A student whose IB subject counts at this level or above meets the rule with any passing grade.

gradeScale.description: The id of the grade scale `minGrade` is measured on, matching a Recognition Scheme's gradeScale.id. Omitted on an ib-subject rule, where the scale is the IB's.

minSubjects.description: For kind 'ib-course-results'. How many graded IB subjects the award must contain for it to qualify. Course Results are not awarded against a fixed shape the way a Diploma is, so a source that accepts them usually says how many subjects it wants to see.

minHigherLevelSubjects.description: For kind 'ib-course-results'. How many of those subjects must be at HL.

alternativeRoute.description: For a rule an applicant cannot satisfy as they stand, the published route that still reaches this Opportunity — supplementary subjects, a retake, a different entry qualification. Only ever the source's own route, never our suggestion, and covered by the same `evidence` as the rule itself. Its reason for existing is that 'you do not meet this' and 'this is closed to you' are different sentences, and a rule that can only say the first of them tells a student to stop when the source did not.

alternativeRouteSummary.description: `alternativeRoute` in one sentence, for lists that show many programmes at once (/guides/course-results/, the finder's card label). Says nothing the long text does not. Programmes whose routes read the same share the same `short`, and a list shows it once.

reachesAtEighteen.description: True when the long text describes a way in without the full Diploma that is open without waiting for an age limit (a supplement, a test anyone may sit). False when every such route waits for an age (typically 21) or none is published, which the long text then says.

operator.description: How to evaluate `alternatives` or the threshold.

alternatives.description: Each element is a set of requirements; satisfying any one set satisfies the rule.

applicability.description: Who and when the rule binds. Without this a rule is not safely usable.

satisfiedBy.description: Named alternative ways to meet it — a language test in place of a subject, for instance.

preparationActions.description: What a student could still do about this gap.

minAverage.description: For kind 'minimum-average': the lowest average on the grade scale named by `gradeScale`. Without `averageOf` it is the qualifying exam's overall average (for an IB Diploma, the total converted by the Recognition Scheme's average table); with it, the average of those subjects' converted grades.

averageOf.description: For kind 'minimum-average': the subjects whose grades are averaged, on a local subject scale — AU's "6.0 in Mathematics A", RUC's "4.0 in the subjects English and Mathematics".

quota.description: For kind 'minimum-average': the admission quota the floor applies to, e.g. "Quota 1". A scoped floor does not decide eligibility — a student below it can still be admitted another way — so the engine reports it beside the outcome rather than as a gap.

shortLabel.description: A shorter label for a card, where the full label is too long to scan — "an English test (IELTS 7.0)". The programme page shows `label`.
